title: Introduce temporal binding validator, KMS proof-of-possession, and audit scrubber for residency pilot
author: Marcus Delgado
release_notes: Adds an opt-in temporal RBAC binding validator, KMS POP verification for operator credentials, and an audit-scrubbing pipeline for residency-sensitive fields. Backward-compatible and behind feature flag.
body: Motivation: We need stronger guarantees that operator/tenant bindings are timeboxed, that operator keys presented to the control plane are proven (KMS POP), and that audit exports do not leak residency-sensitive attributes during the GDPR pilot. This PR introduces three cooperating pieces: 1) a temporal-binding-validator middleware that enforces max-duration and step-down rules for RBAC v2 bindings; 2) KMS-backed proof-of-possession (POP) verification for operator credentials used during delegation flows; 3) an audit-scrubber pipeline that redacts or pseudonymizes residency-related attributes from exported audit rows when the tenant is in pilot mode. Design summary: - Temporal validator: implemented as an admission-style check in the policy-enforcer service. Validates binding metadata: start_ts, expiry_ts, delegation_chain_length, and enforces a configurable per-operator max_ttl. Short-lived bindings can be auto-extended only with a separate approval flow. The validator is feature-flagged (feature.temporal_binding_validator) and defaults to off. - KMS POP verifier: adds a KMS client shim that requests a signed nonce challenge and verifies signatures against tenant CMKs / operator-wrapped keys; supports primary providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and a mock provider for testing. Verification occurs during operator credential registration and when creating operator-scoped temporary bindings. - Audit scrubber: a streaming processor that subscribes to the audit-forwarder topic and applies residency filters for pilot tenants. Redaction rules are pluggable via config/residency_rules.yaml and support pseudonymization (HMAC with tenant salt) or full redaction. The scrubber emits both scrubbed events (for external exports) and retains full events in encrypted internal stores for compliance with retention contracts. Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flags (temporal_binding_validator, kms_pop_verifier, audit_scrubber_pilot). 2) Enable KMS POP in staging for a small set of operator accounts and run POP-only mode (failures logged but not blocking). 3) Enable temporal validator in constrained mode (warnings + non-blocking). 4) Enable scrubber for pilot tenants only. 5) After two weeks of telemetry and a manual compliance review, flip to blocking mode and expand to additional tenants. Backwards compatibility: All behavior is opt-in. Existing bindings and operator flows remain unchanged unless feature flags are toggled. Migration: migration script added to policydb/migrations/20260214_temporal_binding.sql to add max_ttl and issued_at columns and backfill from existing metadata where present. Security considerations: - POP requires KMS IAM roles; the shim includes retry/backoff and safe-fail behavior to avoid large production outages if KMS is throttled. - Scrubber keeps an audit provenance tag (sha256) for each scrubbed row so legal/compliance can rehydrate under strict process. - Unit and integration tests included for edge cases: missing expiry, long delegation chains, KMS transient failure, scrubber rule mismatch. Testing: - New unit tests: 62 files covering validator logic, KMS shim, scrub rules. - Integration test harness: deploys local mock-kms and runs end-to-end binding issuance and audit export flow. - Load test: temporal validator added to perf-canary with lightweight rule set; observed median +1ms added to policy-check path under 1000 RPS. Checklist: - [x] Design doc: docs/security/temporal-binding-validator.md - [x] Migration script added - [x] Feature flags created and documented - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Observability: metrics (validator.rejects, pop.verifications, scrubber.redactions) and traces added - [x] Security review queue: SEC-71 referenced Known limitations: - POP currently supports only RSA/ECDSA keys via KMS sign; hardware-enclave keys (HSM attestation) are TODO. - Scrubber pseudonymization relies on tenant salt; key rotation semantics added to docs but not automated in this PR. Notes: This PR purposefully keeps the scrubber and POP verifications non-blocking initially to gather telemetry and avoid unexpected production failures.

review_comments: Anika Shah: Please add a unit test for the case where expiry_ts is missing and delegation_chain_length > 3. We should reject such bindings in strict mode.
Marcus Delgado: Added missing test and updated validator to log an explicit audit tag when issuing non-blocking warnings.
Priya Nair: KMS shim looks good. Can you add metrics for provider latency (pop.aws.latency_ms) and a circuit-breaker metric?
Marcus Delgado: Added latency histogram and simple circuit-breaker counters. Also added comments about safe-fail semantics in README.
Ethan Cole: Minor: run gofmt/clang-format on provider adapters. Also please include a short runbook for how to escalate KMS POP failures to oncall.
Marcus Delgado: Formatting applied, and runbook stub added at docs/runbooks/kms-pop-failure.md
notes_from_merge: Feature-flagged. Ops: enable kms_pop_verifier in staging for SUP-908 pilot, then enable temporal_binding_validator in warning mode before turning on enforcement. Added an alert on pop.verification.fail_rate>0.5% for 5m.
